scope: Public legal-text versioning and neural-data/neurotechnology legislative metadata; designed to distinguish documented legal causation from temporal correlation
important_distinction: A neural-data metric, metadata event, scientific publication, or technology development occurring before a legal change does not by itself establish that it caused the legal change. Causal claims should require explicit legislative/documentary evidence or a clearly documented causal chain.

current_us_examples.federal_constitution: The National Archives identifies the Constitution and Bill of Rights as foundational documents. 1 U.S.C. §106b establishes the Archivist's publication/certification process when an amendment has been validly adopted.
current_us_examples.illinois_hb2984: Illinois HB2984 (2025-2026) proposed amending BIPA Section 10 to define biometric identifier to include neural data, defining neural data as information generated by measurement of activity of an individual's central or peripheral nervous system and not inferred from non-neural information. The public bill-status record shows the bill was re-referred to Rules on March 27, 2026; it is therefore tracked as proposed, not enacted.

recommended_sources: U.S. House Office of the Historian
BIDS/neurotechnology standards and peer-reviewed literature when relevant to definitions
quality_controls: Use enacted text separately from introduced/proposed text
Record jurisdiction and exact effective date
Distinguish editorial changes from substantive changes
Use official legislative history for causal claims
Do not infer a law change from metadata alone
Do not infer a person's neural activity from legal or technical metadata
security_privacy_boundary: No unauthorized government or legal databases
No claims of causation without documentary evidence
status: Public-source legal-text and neural-data policy change-tracking schema uploaded for research and reproducibility.
